newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes up on tour reports, soy.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes up on tour reports, soy.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher on a surge in CBOT soybeans and on support from results of a crop tour, traders said.
"The reports from the crop tour are that the crop doesn't look that great," a trader said.

The tour of the annual dark northern spring wheat and durum areas of the U.S. pegged 1997 U.S. spring wheat yields at 31.3 bushels per acre, below the 36.4 in 1996. Durum yields were estimated by the tour group at 27.7 bushels per acre, below the 29.7 produced last year.
Traders also said the market was underpinned by USDA's weekly export sales report although the data held little surprise for the spring wheat market.
"There wasn't much in the report for us but it was pretty bullish overall," a trader said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended July 24 totalled 964,300 tonnes, above expectations for 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
MGE spring wheat futures closed three to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 6-3/4 at $3.93.
MGE spring wheat futures volume was estimated by the MGE at 21,434, above the 17,389 traded Wednesday.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to 0.20 cents per cwt lower with September unchanged at $6.20 per cwt.
